step1_analysis.description: This circuit is a differential pair with a tail current source, likely acting as a gain cell in a distributed limiting driver architecture. Note that in the extracted netlist, both input transistors (XM1, XM2) have their drains connected to the same output node (OUTN), which may be an extraction artifact from the original schematic, causing differential AC signals to cancel out.

paper_reference.title: A 3-V Fully Differential Distributed Limiting Driver for 40-Gb/s Optical Transmission Systems

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumption of the driver cell.

paper_reported.value: N/A (Total chip power not explicitly isolated to this cell)

sky130_expected.calculation: Tail current ~ 2mA based on W/L=5/0.5 and VOA=0.8V. Power = 1.8V * 2mA = 3.6mW.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled for a single cell in 1.8V SKY130 process.

sky130_expected.calculation: Due to the netlist topology (both drains to OUTN), the fundamental AC currents cancel out, resulting in near-zero gain. If corrected to a true diff pair, gm * Rload ~ 2mS * 50 = 0.1 (-20dB).
sky130_expected.reasoning: Expected to be very low due to signal cancellation at OUTN in the provided netlist.

bandwidth.description: Operating frequency / bandwidth of the driver.

sky130_expected.calculation: RC time constant at OUTN: R=50 ohm, C ~ 10fF. BW = 1 / (2*pi*R*C) ~ 300 GHz. Practically limited by transistor ft.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 ft is around 40-50GHz, so bandwidth will be limited by device speed.

sky130_expected.calculation: With 2mA tail current and 50 ohm load, max swing is 100mV. Due to cancellation, it will be much lower.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Signal cancellation at OUTN reduces the swing significantly in this specific netlist.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC gain, bandwidth, and transient output swing of the driver cell.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Limiting Driver Testbench
.lib "sky130_fd_pr/models/sky130.lib.spice" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u
.param W_xm3=5u L_xm3=0.5u
.param W_xm4=5u L_xm4=0.5u

XM1 OUTN DINN N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 OUTN DINP N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}
XM3 N1 VOA VSS GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm3} w={W_xm3}
XM4 OUTN OUTN OUTP GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm4} w={W_xm4}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVSS VSS 0 0
VVOA VOA 0 0.8

* 50-ohm loads as described in the paper
R_OUTP VDD OUTP 50
R_OUTN VDD OUTN 50

* Differential Inputs (10 GHz sine wave for transient)
V_DINP DINP 0 dc 0.9 ac 1 sin(0.9 0.2 10G 0 0 0)
V_DINN DINN 0 dc 0.9 ac 1 180 sin(0.9 0.2 10G 0 0 180)

.control
* 1. DC Operating Point & Power
op
let power = -i(VVDD)*1.8
print power

* 2. AC Analysis for Gain and Bandwidth
ac dec 10 1M 100G
let out_diff_mag = mag(v(OUTP) - v(OUTN))
let gain_db = 20*log10(out_diff_mag)
meas ac max_gain max gain_db
meas ac gain_1G find gain_db at=1G
meas ac gain_50G find gain_db at=50G

* 3. Transient Analysis for Output Swing
tran 1p 500p
let vout_diff = v(OUTP) - v(OUTN)
meas tran vout_diff_max max vout_diff
meas tran vout_diff_min min vout_diff
let swing = vout_diff_max - vout_diff_min
print swing

quit
.endc
